openings.claim: Use fixed plywood end stops to make each rod insertion terminate at a repeatable contact plane. This tests the first known parent function alone; it does not establish loaded pointer stability.
openings.delta: Replace operator-selected insertion depth with rod-end contact against captive end blocks in loose crossed plywood channels. Make clearance keepers and hardware captive with the supplied cord or elastic loops, without closing pressure or rod modification. Keep the complete assembly inside 90 mm in every dimension. The nearest rival uses identical channels and captive stops disengaged, with depth set by ruler.
openings.prediction: If insertion-depth variation contributes materially to return error, active stops should reduce unloaded pointer displacement after exchanges compared with ruler-set depth. If clearance, seating angle or rod-size change dominates, depth contact may repeat while pointer error remains or increases. The tighter-fit observation prevents assuming tighter channels improve return.
openings.probe: Within the fabrication allowance, make one fixture with two captive stop positions: active and disengaged. Use only supplied plywood, hardware, tethers and tools; no clamping preload. Within twenty testing minutes, run twelve exchanges per configuration: first five of each original rod, then two exchanges using the 18 mm replacement. Log exchange times and target displacement; apply four ten-second 10 N lateral trials per configuration after exchanges 2, 6, 10 and 12. Compare return and loaded displacement using the target card, ruler and scale. Check captivity and envelope before exchange testing. Fabrication or timing failure leaves the comparison unresolved.
assumptions: Available offcuts, eight bolts and tethers suffice for fixed channels, stops and captive clearance keepers within one hundred fabrication minutes; this is unverified.
Stop contact is observable and comparable across configurations without altering rods.

Defeat conditions include no return improvement, missed 2 mm target, movement during load, any exchange taking forty seconds or more, and failure with the 18 mm rod. Passive channel clearance may prevent meeting the valued outcome.

assessment: A bounded probe of end-contact positioning, with the full return, load, time, captivity and replacement requirements retained. No deployment or reliable performance is claimed. A stop alone does not demonstrate sufficient lateral or angular restraint.
